fields.label: Window (seconds)
fields.description: The length of time over which the call limits are counted. The allowance is refilled every 60 seconds by default.

fields.label: Per-token Rate (calls/window)
fields.description: The steady speed at which a single partner may keep making calls, once any initial burst is used up. An ordinary call and a bulk call each count as one. For example, 120 calls per 60-second window is about two calls every second, on average, sustained. When set to 0, no limit is applied.

fields.label: Per-token Burst (calls)
fields.description: The number of calls a single partner may make in one quick burst before the steady rate takes over. For example, with a rate of 120 per minute and a burst of 240, a partner that has been idle may fire up to 240 calls at once; after that, further calls are allowed only as fast as the rate refills them (about two per second). In short, the burst covers a brief spike, and the rate sets the long-run speed. It is always treated as at least the rate. When left at 0, the default of 240 is used rather than meaning unlimited.

fields.label: Global Rate (calls/window)
fields.description: The steady speed at which all partners together may keep making calls, once any initial burst is used up. For example, 300 calls per 60-second window is about five calls every second, on average, sustained. When set to 0, no limit is applied.

fields.label: Global Burst (calls)
fields.description: The number of calls all partners together may make in one quick burst before the steady global rate takes over. For example, with a global rate of 300 per minute and a burst of 600, up to 600 calls may land at once after a quiet spell; after that, calls are allowed only as fast as the rate refills them. It is always treated as at least the global rate. When left at 0, the default of 600 is used rather than meaning unlimited.

fields.label: Rate limits (bulk calls)
fields.description: Bulk calls are limited separately from ordinary calls. Because a bulk write keeps all of its records locked until it finishes, what is limited here is how many bulk calls may run at the same time, rather than how many are made per minute.

fields.label: Bulk Window (seconds)
fields.description: The length of time over which the bulk-call limit is counted. The allowance is refilled every 5 seconds by default.

fields.label: Bulk Rate (calls/window)
fields.description: The number of bulk calls a single partner is allowed within each bulk window. When set to 0, no limit is applied.

fields.label: Bulk Burst (calls)
fields.description: The number of bulk calls that may run at the same time for a single partner. It is always treated as at least the bulk rate. When left at 0, the default of 1 is used. While it is 1, a second bulk call started at the same moment is refused, which prevents two bulk writes from blocking each other on the same records.

fields.label: Volume limits (rows/day)
fields.description: These limits cap how much data may be moved, separately from how fast. Reads and writes are counted on their own, while ordinary and bulk calls are counted together. Genuine bulk loads are allowed while large-scale scraping is prevented.

fields.label: Volume Window (seconds)
fields.description: The length of time over which the row limits are counted. When left blank, one day (86400 seconds) is used.

fields.label: Per-token Read Rows/window
fields.description: The number of rows a single partner may read within each window, counting ordinary and bulk calls together. When set to 0, no limit is applied.

fields.label: Global Read Rows/window
fields.description: The number of rows that may be read within each window across all partners combined. When set to 0, no limit is applied.

fields.label: Per-token Write Rows/window
fields.description: The number of rows a single partner may create or update within each window, counting ordinary and bulk calls together. When set to 0, no limit is applied.

fields.label: Global Write Rows/window
fields.description: The number of rows that may be created or updated within each window across all partners combined. When set to 0, no limit is applied.

fields.label: Bulk Max Records
fields.description: The largest number of records allowed in a single bulk write. It is kept small on purpose, because a bulk call keeps all of its records locked until it finishes. It cannot be set to 0.

fields.label: Bulk Max Files
fields.description: The largest number of files allowed in a single bulk file upload. Files are limited more tightly than rows because each one is decoded, virus-scanned and saved, which takes about a second. It cannot be set to 0.

fields.label: List Max Page
fields.description: The largest number of records returned by a single read or list call. It cannot be set to 0.

fields.label: List Default Page
fields.description: The number of records returned when the caller does not ask for a specific amount. It cannot be set to 0.

fields.label: File Download Timeout (seconds)
fields.description: The number of seconds the server waits while fetching a file from a partner-supplied link before it gives up. It cannot be set to 0.

fields.label: File Download Max Size (MB)
fields.description: The largest file size, in megabytes, that is accepted when a file is fetched from a partner-supplied link. A larger file is refused. It cannot be set to 0.

fields.label: Idempotency Window (hours)
fields.description: The number of hours a request's idempotency key and its saved response are kept, so that a repeat of the same request is answered from the saved response instead of being written again. It applies only when a request asks for it.

fields.label: Async bulk jobs
fields.description: A second, asynchronous tier for high-volume creates. A partner submits a job, it is queued and drained by a dedicated background worker, and completion is reported by a webhook and a status endpoint. The tier stays dormant until it is switched on.

fields.label: Inline Job Max Records
fields.description: The largest number of records accepted in a single inline-JSON job.

fields.label: File Job Max Records
fields.description: The largest number of records accepted in a single uploaded CSV or JSONL file job. A larger file is refused.

fields.label: File Job Max Size (MB)
fields.description: The largest size, in megabytes, accepted for a single uploaded file job. A larger upload is refused before it is stored.

fields.label: Jobs Processed At Once
fields.description: The number of jobs the background worker processes at the same time. It is held at one so bulk creates run serially.

fields.label: Concurrent Jobs Per Partner
fields.description: The number of jobs a single partner may have queued or running at once. A further submission is refused until one finishes.

fields.label: Max Queued Jobs
fields.description: The largest number of jobs that may be queued or running across all partners. A submission beyond this is refused and asked to retry later.

fields.label: Chunk Size
fields.description: The number of records the worker commits in a single transaction while draining a job.

fields.label: Job Timeout (seconds)
fields.description: The number of seconds a single job may run on the background worker before it is stopped. A job still marked in-progress past this window is treated as stranded — its worker died — and is failed by the reaper.

fields.label: Results Retention (days)
fields.description: The number of days a finished job and its per-record results are kept before they are purged.

fields.label: Async bulk volume
fields.description: How many rows the async tier may move per day, kept separate from the synchronous quota so a backfill cannot drain the interactive budget.

fields.label: Per-token Async Rows/day
fields.description: The number of rows a single partner may write per day through the async tier.

fields.label: Global Async Rows/day
fields.description: The number of rows written per day across all partners through the async tier.
